bugs.summary: Derived struct deserialization fails to skip unknown object-valued or array-valued fields. Because ignored_any is forwarded to deserialize_any, only the container header is consumed and nested entries are treated as subsequent outer fields, causing a later required field to be lost or misread.
bugs.match_rule: A report must claim that ordinary Serde unknown-field handling leaves the contents of an ignored nested object or array unread and consequently misaligns later fields of a derived struct.

bugs.summary: Tape Value get_array, get_object, try_get_array and try_get_object slice the tape one node short, losing the last element of a nested container.
bugs.match_rule: Names the off-by-one slice idx..idx+count in the tape shortcut accessors (container header plus count nodes), dropping the last element or leaving an empty slice that later panics on empty containers.
bugs.caveat: Kept as wrong-behavior, but the panics on empty containers are a crash from valid input on the same defect; a finding that reports only that panic should score here. Shared code.

bugs.summary: Long decimals are corrupted because a byte value is used as an index when digit_count is corrected.
bugs.match_rule: Names `start_digits = get!(buf, start) as usize` in the float path, which stores the byte at start rather than the offset, so the leading-zero digit_count correction is wrong and long decimals get a wrong value.
bugs.caveat: Listed as a possible crash, but it gives a wrong value and did not panic in any run. Shared code.

bugs.summary: Huge exponents wrap through `as i32` and give wrong finite numbers, while valid very long exponents are rejected.
bugs.match_rule: Names narrowing the accumulated i64 exponent with `as i32` (wrapping into range and giving a wrong finite value) or the error on exponents past 2^32 rejecting valid numbers, in the default number parser.
bugs.caveat: Upstream fix is co-authored by Claude. Shared code.

bugs.summary: A NUL byte counts as structural-or-whitespace, so a number followed by NUL is accepted.
bugs.match_rule: Names the STRUCTURAL_OR_WHITESPACE tables treating byte 0 as a valid terminator (tied to zero padding of the input buffer), so number parsing accepts an embedded NUL after a number.
bugs.caveat: Listed as a possible crash, but it does not panic. The tag has a test that asserts this behaviour with a todo comment, so upstream knew. Shared code.

bugs.summary: Fixed-length serde targets leave unread array elements on the tape, which are then read as later values.
bugs.match_rule: Names the serde array path handing a visitor CommaSeparated without checking afterward that all elements were consumed, so surplus elements shift into later fields of a tuple, array or struct target.
bugs.caveat: Upstream fix is co-authored by Claude. Shared code.

bugs.summary: A lone high surrogate such as "\ud800" parses as NUL (U+0000) instead of returning an error.
bugs.match_rule: Names get_unicode_codepoint returning Ok((0, _)) for a high surrogate without a following low surrogate, a leftover failure sentinel that callers now take as code point 0, silently decoding it as NUL.
bugs.caveat: RFC 8259 section 8.2 only says lone surrogates give unpredictable behaviour; the wrong part is silent NUL where the crate rejects the low-surrogate twin. Upstream fix is co-authored by Claude. Parse_str differs per backend but this function is shared; run on NEON. `"\ud800\uzzzz"` already errored here on NEON through another check.

bugs.summary: Serializing an empty Vec with simd_json::to_string emits only an opening bracket. SerializeSeq::end returns successfully while first is still true, leaving the empty array unterminated; nesting the empty Vec also produces malformed JSON.
bugs.match_rule: A report must identify empty known-length sequences, such as Vec::<u8>::new(), as emitting an unterminated array because SerializeSeq::end skips the closing bracket when first is true.
